title: Middle Three Elements
description:
Write a function `middle_three(items)` that returns the middle three elements of a list of odd length >= 3 as a new list.
If `len(items) < 3`, return an empty list `[]`.
Your function must not mutate or alter the original input list.

hidden_tests.kind: a list with 7 elements checking mutation

hints: Slicing in Python requires careful midpoint calculation, and destructive methods should be avoided.
Look at your midpoint index and slice upper bound: in [start:end], the item at index 'end' is not included.
If you calculate mid = len(items) // 2, slicing mid-1 to mid+1 only captures two elements instead of three.
Use items[mid - 1 : mid + 2] to extract precisely 3 items, and ensure you do not call .pop() on the input.
